en: The Dhāraṇī of the Name of Mārīcī: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Goddess Mārīcī!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī.

In the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of monks—numbering thirteen hundred and fifty monks—and many great śrāvakas and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the Blessed One addressed the monks there:
"Monks, there is a deity named Mārīcī; she follows close behind the sun and the moon."
She is not seen, not grasped, not bound, not obstructed, not opposed, not robbed, not deluded, not punished, not shorn, and not burned; nor does she fall into the power of an enemy.
Monks, even one who knows the name of that goddess called Mārīcī is likewise not seen, not grasped, not bound, not obstructed, not opposed, not robbed, not deluded, not punished, and not shorn.
He is not burned, nor does he fall into the power of an enemy.
Monks, I know the name of this goddess Mārīcī;
I, too, am not seen, not bound, not ceased, not opposed, not deluded, not punished, not shaven, not burned, and do not fall into the power of an enemy.
These are the mantra words:
namely, *oṃ padākramasi parākramasi udayamasi nairamasi arkamasi markamasi urmasi vanamasi gulmamasi cīvaramasi mahācīvaramasi antardhānamasi svāhā*.
Oṃ! Goddess Mārīcī, protect me on the path; protect me from the wrong path;
protect me from the fear of men.
Protect me from the fear of kings; protect me from the fear of elephants;
protect me from the fear of thieves.
Protect me from the fear of nāgas; protect me from the fear of lions;
protect me from the fear of tigers.
Protect me from the fear of horses;
protect me from the fear of fire;
protect me from the fear of water.
Protect me from the fear of snakes;
protect me from the fear of poison;
protect me from the fear of all adversaries and enemies.
Protect me amidst the agitated;
protect me amidst the unagitated;
protect me amidst those who have fainted.
Protect me from those who are not intoxicated;
guard me from the one who has not arrived;
guard me from the fierce beast.
Protect, protect me and all sentient beings from all the wicked and malicious!
Namely: Homage to the Triple Gem! Oṃ ālo tālo kālo sacchalo satvamudrati! Protect, protect me and my retinue, as well as all sentient beings, from all fears and calamities!
Svāhā! Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the Blessed Noble Goddess Mārīcī!
I shall now recite her heart mantra:
namely, *oṃ vattālī vadālī varālī varāhamukhī*.
Bind, bind the eyes and mouths of all the wicked and malicious ones! Bind their mouths! Render them dazed, paralyze them, and delude them! Svāhā!
Oṃ, to Mārīcī, svāhā!

Oṃ varālī vadālī vattālī varāhamukhī! Bind, bind the eyes and mouths of all the wicked and malicious ones; yawn, yawn; paralyze, paralyze; delude, delude; shatter, shatter; threaten, threaten! Hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Oṃ, to Mārīcī: move, move! faint, faint! become utterly bewildered, become utterly bewildered! depart, depart! may all wicked beings on the path or off the path, and all obstacles and hindering spirits, depart; let them not remain! by the truth of the Three Jewels, svāhā!
Oṃ, fierce one, most fierce one, svāhā!
Oṃ agali pagali pañcagali, bind, bind the body, speech, and mind, and the mouth and eyes of all the wicked and extremely wicked ones! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!

The Blessed One spoke this, and the monks, those bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas—rejoiced and approved of what the Blessed One had said.
The Noble Dhāraṇī named Mārīcī is completed.
